tldr: Markets stabilized Friday (S&P +0.31%, Nasdaq +1.09%) even as a hot October NFP (+165K vs 65K consensus, unemployment 4.1%) cemented a December Fed hike (odds now ~77-80%) -- an oversold bounce (CNN Fear & Greed ~21 Extreme Fear, McClellan -111.5 washout), not a resolved risk picture.

The AI-capex political backlash that triggered Thursday's -4.36%/-5.52% rout has spread beyond Texas to Georgia, Ohio and Virginia, with UBS/Goldman estimating 30-45% of 2028 US data-center capacity now at risk -- yet hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Oracle) haven't cut 2026 capex guidance.

Biggest risk to the book: the levered silver/gold-miner sleeve now trades with equity-correlated beta (Goldman cut its 2026 gold target to ,150 from ,650 on the hawkish Fed) and HK tech (Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi) is trading as a pure AI-capex-sentiment proxy, down in sympathy Friday despite Southbound flows flipping back to buying.

China's rare-earth export-control truce expires Tuesday Nov 10 with no renewal notice yet -- the single highest-impact near-term catalyst for the MP/Lynas/Energy Fuels/USA Rare Earth basket, complicated by a new "subpoena season" political overhang on MP's own government equity stake.

Smart-money overlap: Pelosi's household bought NVDA call options (largest purchase in 3 years) right into the Friday chip bounce; Congress also piled into CSCO (most-bought ticker across 38 members in 30 days) as an AI-infrastructure picks-and-shovels play.

SGX read: OCBC beat and raised 2026 guidance -- the only one of the three banks to do so -- while DBS and UOB both missed on weaker trading income, a relative-strength signal within the owner's largest exposure.

regime.label: Hot jobs meet a hawkish Fed and an AI-capex political shock -- two-way whipsaw, oversold bounce
regime.oneLiner: Friday's chip-led bounce and a blowout NFP print both argue the market is doing some healing on its own, but Extreme Fear sentiment and a McClellan washout look like an oversold bounce, not resolution -- the December rate hike is now all but cemented and the AI-capex political fight is spreading, not resolving.

topNews.headline: October US payrolls smash estimates at +165K, unemployment falls to 4.1%
topNews.actionable: A strong jobs beat plus hot wage growth reinforces the hawkish Fed narrative that already drove Goldman to cut its gold forecast -- expect near-term pressure on bullion even though miners have structural momentum.

topNews.headline: US stocks stage partial rebound as chip stocks bounce, but Nasdaq stays in correction
topNews.actionable: The bounce is a relief rally within a correction, not a reversal -- wait for AMAT's Nov 12 earnings to confirm whether AI-capex demand is actually intact.

topNews.actionable: November 10 is the single highest-impact date on the rare-earth watchlist this month -- a lapse into tighter Chinese export controls would be a direct bullish catalyst for MP, UUUU and Lynas versus Chinese processors like 6680.HK.

topNews.actionable: Government-backed rare-earth plays now carry a real political-overhang risk heading into 2027 committee season.

topNews.actionable: OCBC's guidance raise is a relative-strength signal within the SGX bank trio -- on any further regional risk-off dip, OCBC looks like the preferred name to deploy cash into.
